channel.title: Global Competition Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Competition Review (globalcompetitionreview.com)

item.title: China’s Sinochem offers ‘structured’ foreign investment proposal over Pirelli stake
item.description: Chinese state-owned conglomerate Sinochem has proposed measures to mitigate foreign investment risks related to its controlling stake in Pirelli, but the company’s influence could still face scrutiny in the US and Italy.

item.title: CMA proposes first-ever conduct requirements under DMCC
item.description: News publishers and consumer groups have welcomed the UK Competition and Markets Authority’s first proposed behavioural remedies under its new digital market regime to police Google’s artificial intelligence feature in its search results, but warned content providers still need adequate remuneration.

item.title: Against the grain: The Tipline for 28 January 2026
item.description: Union Pacific’s antitrust problems do not end with its acquisition of Norfolk Southern. A lawsuit filed by farmers and a rival railroad on Tuesday accused the rail giant of monopolising shipments of grain by levying extreme fees on customers who wanted to use a more direct route. Also in Tipline, a camera technology startup accused Apple of copying and killing its product.

item.title: FTC suit ignores retailers’ sway, adhesive companies say
item.description: The Federal Trade Commission’s challenge to Henkel AG/A-Paint disregards the "significant power” of a small set of retailers to dictate which construction adhesives appear before customers, the merging parties have argued.

item.title: On mute: The Briefing for 29 January 2026
item.description: The UK government continues to resist invitations to debate the merits of Netflix’s proposed $83 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Responding to a written question in the House of Lords today, a Labour peer said it is not “appropriate” to comment on “any live or potential” merger involving Warner Bros or any other US company. Also in The Briefing, Ursula von der Leyen warns competition rules mus...

item.title: Meta complainant voices concerns about new WhatsApp pricing policy in Italy
item.description: Meta’s new plans to charge rival artificial intelligence chatbots to access WhatsApp in Italy are another way of harming competition, potentially making the app an “unviable channel” for most competitors, a Spanish AI assistant company has said.

item.title: Judge challenges ‘bizarre’ Jeld-Wen appeal
item.description: A federal appellate judge has questioned doormaker Jeld-Wen’s effort to avoid a court-ordered divestiture as a request to make plaintiff Steves & Sons prove its successful merger case “all over again”.

item.title: First whistleblower reward sparks race to report, lawyers say
item.description: The Department of Justice’s swift issuance of its first antitrust whistleblower reward shows the enforcer is prioritising its new criminal enforcement weapon, according to members of the antitrust bar.

item.title: Assefi: “Frenzy“ of whistleblowers approaching DOJ
item.description: The new whistleblower regime at the Department of Justice’s antitrust division has sparked a “massive effect on case generation”, deputy assistant attorney general Omeed Assefi has said.

item.title: Striking distance: The Tipline for 29 January 2026
item.description: The Lone Star State certainly has an independent streak but it is not going it alone with respect to restraints of trade impacting government procurement. Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton revealed on Thursday that the state had joined the Procurement Collusion Strike Force of the Department of Justice’s antitrust division.
